rows.question: What documents are needed for an uncontested divorce intake?
rows.answer: Documents needed for an uncontested divorce intake. An uncontested divorce turns on both spouses agreeing on property, custody, and support. The intake cannot be completed until the firm has: 1. A copy of the marriage certificate. 2. A completed financial affidavit from each spouse, listing income, debts, and monthly expenses. 3. A property list covering the family home, vehicles, bank accounts, retirement accounts, and any debts in either spouse's name. 4. A draft parenting plan, if the couple has minor children, covering custody, visitation, and child support. 5. A signed intake form with current contact details for both spouses. rows.question: How does a free consultation start?
rows.answer: How a free consultation starts. A free consultation starts by phone call, by email, or through the contact form on the firm's website. The caller is asked for their name, a phone number, the type of matter, and a short description of the issue. [02-consultation-process.md (chunk 3)] Sample fee schedule. - Free initial consultation: no charge, up to 30 minutes. - Uncontested divorce, flat fee: $1,500, payable in two instalments — $750 at engagement and $750 before filing. - Document review, hourly: $200 per hour, billed in 15-minute units. - All fees are confirmed in writing in the engagement letter before any work begins. No work is billed before the engagement letter is signed. [03-fee-policy.md (chunk 6)]

rows.question: What should a client bring to the first consultation?
rows.answer: What to bring to the first consultation. Clients should bring photo identification, any court papers they have already received, and the documents listed on the intake checklist for their matter. For a divorce consultation, that means the marriage certificate and the financial affidavit, if they have them already. Bringing the documents to the first meeting saves a second round of chasing them later. [02-consultation-process.md (chunk 4)] What happens in the consultation. An attorney personally evaluates the case in the consultation and explains the options, the likely steps, and the fee. No legal advice is given before the consultation, and no advice is given by phone or email to someone who is not yet a client. After the consultation, the client receives a written summary of the options discussed and the next steps if they choose to proceed. [02-consultation-process.md (chunk 5)]

rows.question: What is the flat fee for an uncontested divorce?
rows.answer: What the flat fee covers. The uncontested divorce flat fee covers the intake review, drafting of the petition and settlement agreement, and filing with the court. It does not cover a contested hearing, mediation, or an appeal. If a case becomes contested, the firm quotes a new fee in writing before continuing. rows.question: How quickly does the firm respond to a new inquiry?
rows.answer: Response times. The firm responds to a new inquiry within one business day. Existing clients receive a response to a message within two business days. Urgent messages — for example, a court date within 7 days — are flagged for same-day review by the attorney handling the case. [04-deadline-policy.md (chunk 8)] What the flat fee covers. The uncontested divorce flat fee covers the intake review, drafting of the petition and settlement agreement, and filing with the court. It does not cover a contested hearing, mediation, or an appeal. If a case becomes contested, the firm quotes a new fee in writing before continuing. [03-fee-policy.md (chunk 7)]

rows.question: Are client documents stored locally or in the cloud?
rows.answer: Where client documents are stored. Client documents are stored locally, on the firm's own office systems. Nothing is uploaded to a public cloud service and nothing is sent to an outside AI service. Documents are stored in the firm's case files, and access is limited to the attorney and paralegal assigned to the case. [05-confidentiality.md (chunk 11)] Who can see a client's file. Only the attorney and paralegal assigned to the case can open a client's file. No other staff member, and no outside party, is given access unless the client gives written permission or a court orders it. [05-confidentiality.md (chunk 12)]

rows.question: What cases does the firm not take on?
rows.answer: Matters outside the firm's practice. The firm handles family law and estate planning only. It does not take on criminal defence, personal injury, immigration, or bankruptcy cases. A caller with one of those matters is given the name of the local bar association referral service instead of a consultation. [06-what-we-do-not-do.md (chunk 14)] What the firm will not do. The firm will not give legal advice by phone or email to someone who is not yet a client. It will not quote a fee for a matter it does not handle, and it will not confirm a deadline for a case it has not reviewed. Any caller asking for one of those things is asked to book a consultation or to contact the appropriate service. [06-what-we-do-not-do.md (chunk 15)]
